situation: Our team needed to get a new microservice built and released into production in a timely manner.
task: Own the process for managing the moving pieces to build and release a Billing (.NET) microservice into production.
action: Refined stories, followed up with stakeholders and team members on action items, rallied team members around a common goal, provided updates to leadership and stakeholders, uncovered gotchas and technical road blocks along the way, became the voice of the team for all things related to billing service
result: The billing service was launched to production within the quoted timeframe with minimal bugs and fast follow ups for continued support.

title: Spearheading the JavaScript-to-TypeScript migration at Monolith Forensics
questionPatterns: Tell me about a time you drove a technical change
How have you influenced technical direction?
Tell me about a large refactor or migration
situation: Both front and backend code that supported the Monolith SPA was still in vanilla JavaScript when I was hired
task: Modernize and harden the stack by converting both front and backend codebases into TypeScript
action: Updated the configuration infrastructure to support TypeScript in the back and frontend repositories, it included re-configuring already existing legacy code and introducing interfaces and types throughout.
result: A vast majority of both codebases had typing support, this greatly supported new code and drastically reduced bugs throughout the platform.

title: Mentoring engineers at Monolith Forensics and Cart.com
questionPatterns: Tell me about a time you mentored someone
How do you help teammates grow?
situation: Monolith - The first dev hire was a Junior, it was his first job in the industry and I helped him learn things like unit testing, proper code reviews, keeping modules concise, TypeScript types, abstracting only where necessary, performance improvements, debugging tools like chrome dev tools and debugger mode in an IDE.  Cart - helped new team members onboard, helped team members with understanding various microservices.
task: Help existing Junior team members grow into more advanced programmers.  Help new team members onboard and integrate faster.
action: Guiding through code reviews, one on one meetings, work chat app calls, provide spec documents, refine user stories
result: Upskilled existing junior engineers and ramped up new team members to be able to start contributing features faster.
